capability_review.scope: post-finalization diagnosis; no model or tool decision
capability_review.overall_assessment: This finalized forecast run moved from a 0.779 baseline to 0.138 validation / 0.130 holdout via a measured feature-engineering sequence (date/time decomposition, categorical frequency, rolling history aggregates, target and keyed target encodings) and a weighted blend of three GBM families plus a linear model. Every feature step was measured (transform 0.230 → frequency 0.211 → history 0.159 → target encoding 0.141 → grouped history 0.137), and further attempts (interaction transforms at 0.395, trend/dev at 0.149, several history variants) did not help. Because the plateau is consistent across both feature and model-family dimensions, and the shipped blend's validation score is not better than the best single model, the evidence does not establish any tool, agent, contract, or model-selection shortcoming. The limiting factor appears to be the task's inherent predictability ceiling plus diminishing returns of feature engineering — no demonstrated generic gap. Main risks for owner review remain retroactive selection via the internal holdout (not a basis for shipping) and serve-time recomputation of lag/target-derived aggregates to avoid out-of-time leakage.

findings.title: Feature/model plateau reflects diminishing returns; no tool or contract gap demonstrated
findings.generic_capability: The run already expressed and measured the generic operations needed to reach baseline-to-competitive gains: date/time decomposition and calendar transforms, categorical frequency encoding, rolling history aggregates over configurable windows, target encoding (global and keyed/interaction), and blending multiple gradient-boosting families plus a linear model.
findings.why_existing_tools_insufficient: The available tools were sufficient: the shipped configuration and all competitive models were produced entirely by the existing transform, frequency, history, target-encoding, and blending tools, and the measuring scaffold recorded scores after every step. No useful generic operation was shown to be unexpressible; failed probes (interaction transform at 0.395, trend/dev at 0.149, several grouped-history variants above 0.137) were expressible and simply did not help, so they do not prove a capability or tool gap.
findings.alternative_explanation: The ~0.137 plateau is best explained by the inherent predictability ceiling of the task (retail demand noise, closed-store regime) and by cold-start effects in the rolling-history features on the earliest temporal window, rather than by any missing primitives. The large gap between internal cross-validation (e.g., e2 CV 0.244) and the time-split validation (0.137) reflects rolling-history features degrading on early folds, not a tool defect.
findings.leakage_or_serving_risk: Target-encoding and rolling-aggregate features must be computed strictly on past training data and recomputed identically at serving time; a leak would inflate validation, but the slightly negative optimism of the shipped blend and catboost runs is not evidence of such a leak and should be confirmed by an owner review of the feature-lag derivation.
findings.testable_hypothesis: A follow-up evaluation with a distinct temporal holdout, using strictly lag-only feature recomputation at serve time, would reproduce a validation metric within a few points of ~0.137 across the same GBM families; if it does, no capability gap exists and remaining gains come only from data/task limits. New evidence (e.g., a live/lagged serving evaluation) is required before any product change.
